experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, fresh pasta, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and street food stalls. This bohemian neighborhood offers the most authentic Roman culinary experience away from tourist traps.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a baroque villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited to 360 visitors at a time, ensuring an unhurried, immersive experience with masterpieces like Apollo and Daphne.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, cured meats, and the famously divisive quinto quarto (offal dishes) that define true Roman cucina povera tradition.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Forum and Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. Combined with Colosseum entry, this archaeological complex offers unparalleled insight into Roman history and culture, with panoramic views over ruins that inspired Renaissance artists for centuries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get oriented in your room.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the local area near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the nearby streets of Rome, GA and pick up any essentials from a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on budget-friendly snacks and drinks for the week.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Meal on the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near Chateau Drive area (~$8-12) for a quick, affordable first-night meal after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Lay out your week's plan, charge all devices, and get a good night's sleep. Check if the hotel offers a free continental breakfast for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Start with the hotel's complimentary continental breakfast if available. Head to Downtown Rome, GA (about 10-15 min drive) and visit the historic Clock Tower and Broad Street area. Walk the charming downtown strip, admire the public murals and local art installations, and stop by the Rome Area History Museum (free or low-cost entry) to learn about the city's rich heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (a National Historic Landmark, ~$5 entry) to explore Native American and Civil War history through art and artifacts. Afterward, stroll along the Oostanaula River waterfront and enjoy the scenic views. Browse local antique shops and galleries along Broad Street for unique, affordable art finds.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local food scene on Broad Street. Rome, GA has a growing arts and dining scene with several budget-friendly options. Walk around and enjoy the warm June evening (around 29°C) before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast (free if available) or grab a coffee and pastry at a local café downtown (~$5)
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café or a local deli on Broad Street (~$10-14) for a fresh, affordable lunch
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant or a similar local spot in downtown Rome (~$12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing — June highs near 30°C can feel intense. Carry a reusable water bottle. Check local event listings; downtown Rome often hosts free outdoor events and art walks in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Shorter University campus and its beautiful grounds, which feature public art and historic architecture open to visitors. Then head to the Rome City Auditorium area and explore any current exhibitions at local community art spaces. Pick up a free local arts and events guide from a downtown shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or rideshare to the Berry College campus (about 10-15 min from downtown) — one of the largest college campuses in the world by acreage. The grounds are stunning, free to visit, and feature beautiful Gothic-style architecture, wildlife (including deer and eagles), and scenic walking trails. A perfect blend of natural beauty and architectural art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Rome for a Friday evening out. Check if any local galleries are hosting a free opening or art walk event. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Broad Street on a Friday night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bakery (~$5-7)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local grocery store (Kroger or Publix nearby, ~$6-8) and enjoy it on the Berry College grounds
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli or a local pizza spot in downtown Rome (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is free to visit but respect campus rules and wildlife. Bring sunscreen and a hat for outdoor exploration in the afternoon heat. Friday evenings often have live music or pop-up events downtown.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Coosa Valley or explore the Etowah Indian Mounds State Historic Site in Cartersville (~45 min drive, ~$5 entry). This remarkable archaeological site features ancient Native American earthwork mounds and a museum with fascinating artifacts — a true open-air art and history experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at Red Top Mountain State Park (~40 min from Rome) for a scenic afternoon hike along Lake Allatoona. The trails offer beautiful views and a refreshing escape from the city heat. Swimming is available at the beach area for a small fee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome and treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Relax at the hotel and plan the second half of your week.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a drive-through coffee and sandwich (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the grocery store for the day trip (~$7-10) — picnic at the mounds or the park
meals.dinner: Applebee's or Texas Roadhouse near the hotel area (~$14-18 per person) for a satisfying sit-down meal

day_by_day.notes: Start early to beat the heat — aim to be at Etowah Mounds by 9:00 AM. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and insect repellent for outdoor sites. Check opening hours for Etowah Mounds (typically closed Mondays/Tuesdays). Gas costs for the day trip: budget ~$10-15.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome Farmers Market (check local listings for Sunday hours and location) to experience local produce, handmade crafts, and artisan food vendors. This is a great way to sample local flavors on a budget and pick up unique, affordable souvenirs. Chat with local vendors and artists about the Rome, GA creative community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring the Coosa River Bicentennial Trail and the scenic riverside parks. Visit the iconic Three Rivers monument at the confluence of the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers (free). Rent a bike if available locally for a fun, budget-friendly way to cover more ground along the river trail.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using fresh ingredients purchased at the farmers market, using the hotel's microwave or any available kitchen facilities. Alternatively, enjoy a casual Sunday dinner at a local family restaurant. Spend the evening reviewing photos and journaling about your trip so far.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries, fruit, and coffee purchased at the farmers market (~$6-9)
meals.lunch: Street food or a food truck at the farmers market (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Simple self-catered meal from market ingredients (~$8-10) or Cracker Barrel near the hotel (~$12-15)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday can be quieter in terms of attractions — lean into the relaxed pace. The farmers market is a highlight for food and art lovers. Stay hydrated throughout the day; June Sundays can be particularly warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a self-guided photography and street art walk through Rome's neighborhoods. Document the city's murals, historic architecture, and everyday life. Visit the Rome-Floyd County Library which sometimes hosts free art exhibitions and cultural events. Check their calendar in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Cave Spring, GA (~20 min from Rome) — a charming small town with a natural limestone cave (Rolater Park, ~$3 entry), a natural spring, and a beautiful historic downtown. The cave is a unique and cool (literally — caves stay around 60°F/15°C) afternoon escape from the summer heat. Browse the antique shops and small galleries in Cave Spring's quaint downtown.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a final weeknight dinner. Explore any part of downtown you haven't visited yet. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs or local art prints from downtown shops.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local coffee shop (~$5-7)
meals.lunch: A local sandwich shop or sub place in Rome before heading to Cave Spring (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Broad Street Brewing or a local gastropub in downtown Rome for a relaxed Monday evening (~$13-17)

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring's Rolater Park is a hidden gem — arrive early afternoon to avoid any small crowds. The cave tour is short but memorable and provides welcome relief from the heat. Bring a light jacket for the cave visit despite the warm outdoor temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast. Take one last walk through your favorite spot in Rome — whether that's the Broad Street downtown strip, the riverside trail, or the Berry College grounds. Visit any attraction or shop you may have missed during the week. Pick up any final souvenirs or local food items to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel to pack and check out. Depending on your departure time, grab a final lunch in Rome before heading to the airport or beginning your journey home. Reflect on the week's experiences and the art, food, and culture you've discovered.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home or continue to next destination. If your flight is in the evening, spend remaining time relaxing at the hotel or a nearby café.

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast (final use — make it count!) or a local favorite café (~$6-9)
meals.lunch: A farewell meal at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip (~$10-15)
meals.dinner: Airport food or travel meal depending on departure schedule (~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the hotel. Keep receipts organized for any expense tracking. Total estimated daily food budget: $25-40/day. Total estimated week food budget: $175-280. Look for any loyalty points or rewards from the La Quinta stay before departing.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (15 Chateau Drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings and shake off any travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – Join a guided evening walk through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, local wines, and other Roman street bites. A perfect, low-effort introduction to Roman cuisine after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit (grab something at the airport if needed)
meals.dinner: Covered as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk; snacks and tastings included. Supplement with a gelato from a local gelateria afterward (~€3–5).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk in advance as evening slots fill quickly in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes. June evenings average around 20–22°C – a light jacket is handy. Keep spending light on Day 1 to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Start early (pre-booked timed entry for 09:00) to beat the crowds and the midday heat (highs near 30°C). Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections, from the Gallery of Maps to the Raphael Rooms, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo and the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade. Rest in the shade of a nearby café during the hottest part of the day (14:00–16:00). Then wander through the Prati neighborhood, known for its elegant streets and excellent mid-range eateries.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the Ponte Sant'Angelo at sunset for iconic views, then head to a traditional Roman trattoria in Prati for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – cornetto and cappuccino (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria, Prati) – Rome's legendary pizza al taglio spot; try multiple toppings (~€10–14 per person)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Il Sorpasso (Prati area) – mid-range Roman classics like cacio e pepe and saltimbocca (~€25–35 per person including wine)

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be pre-booked online (vatican.va) – walk-up queues can be 2–3 hours. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Sistine Chapel. Carry a refillable water bottle; Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Pre-booked timed entry (mandatory; only 360 visitors per 2-hour slot). Arrive at 09:00 for the first slot to enjoy Bernini's stunning sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in an intimate villa setting. Afterward, take a relaxing walk through the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain area on foot. Visit the Pantheon (book timed entry online, ~€5) – one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Browse the boutiques and artisan shops around Piazza Navona.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy aperitivo hour (18:00–20:00) at a bar near Piazza Navona – a quintessential Roman ritual with free snacks included with your drink. Then dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel – cornetto integrale and a macchiato (~€4)
meals.lunch: Osteria dell'Ingegno (near Pantheon) – fresh pasta and Roman antipasti in a relaxed setting (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Ristorante da Francesco (Piazza del Fico, near Piazza Navona) – beloved local spot for thin-crust Roman pizza and pasta (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be reserved weeks in advance at galleriaborghese.it – this is non-negotiable. The gallery is a 20-minute walk or short bus ride from the hotel area. Afternoon heat will be intense (~30°C); the Pantheon's interior is naturally cool – a great midday refuge.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Arrive at opening time (09:00) to explore the ancient heart of the Roman Empire before the heat peaks. Walk through the Forum where Julius Caesar was cremated, climb Palatine Hill for panoramic views over the ruins, and imagine emperors and senators at work. Allow 3–3.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Circus Maximus and then cool off with a long lunch. Afterward, explore the Aventine Hill neighborhood – visit the Knights of Malta keyhole (a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome) and the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Testaccio neighborhood evening – explore Rome's most authentic working-class district on foot, stopping at local bars and enjoying the lively Saturday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at a bar near the Forum – espresso and a tramezzino (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) – iconic Roman trattoria famous for rigatoni alla pajata and coda alla vaccinara (~€28–38 per person)
meals.dinner: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina (Via dei Giubbonari) – celebrated deli-restaurant hybrid; perfect for a charcuterie board, cheese, and a glass of natural wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum, Palatine Hill, and Roman Forum share a combined ticket (~€16–18); book online at coopculture.it to skip queues. Wear a hat and sunscreen – the Forum has almost no shade. Saturday evenings in Testaccio are lively; reservations recommended at Flavio al Velavevodetto.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Join a guided offal and street food tour to taste supplì, porchetta, artichokes, and traditional Roman offal dishes (pajata, trippa). A fascinating deep-dive into cucina povera culture. Markets are especially vibrant on Sunday mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pyramid of Cestius (a surprising ancient Egyptian-style tomb in the middle of Rome) and the nearby Protestant Cemetery, where Keats and Shelley are buried – a peaceful, shaded retreat. Then head to the Trastevere neighborhood for a slow afternoon wander through its medieval lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on a rooftop bar in Trastevere, followed by dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Tastings included in the Testaccio Market Food Tour (supplì, porchetta, local cheeses)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Trastevere café – bruschetta, burrata, and a glass of house white (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) – beloved neighborhood trattoria with Roman classics like cacio e pepe and tiramisu; book ahead (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market Food Tour should be pre-booked; Sunday morning is the best time to visit as locals shop for the week. Trastevere is extremely popular on Sunday evenings – make dinner reservations at Da Enzo al 29 well in advance. Carry cash for market vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but stunning Capitoline Museums (Musei Capitolini) – the world's oldest public museums, housing Marcus Aurelius's original bronze equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and breathtaking views over the Roman Forum from the terrace. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Jewish Ghetto – one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhoods. Visit the Great Synagogue of Rome (with its small museum), browse artisan shops, and explore Campo de' Fiori market (winds down by 14:00 on weekdays). Take a mid-afternoon break at a café to escape the peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Final art experience: visit the Doria Pamphilj Gallery (open until 19:00) – a private palazzo gallery with Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. Then a farewell dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café – yogurt, fruit, and espresso (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Nonna Betta (Jewish Ghetto) – specializing in Roman-Jewish cuisine; try carciofi alla giudia (deep-fried artichokes) and baccalà (~€22–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Osteria Barberini (near Piazza Barberini) – elegant but mid-range Roman cuisine; perfect for a special last full evening meal (~€35–45 per person with wine)

day_by_day.notes: Capitoline Museums are closed on Mondays – double-check opening hours and book online. Doria Pamphilj Gallery is a hidden gem that many tourists miss; the audio guide narrated by a Pamphilj family member is charming and included. June 21 is the summer solstice – the longest day of the year, so enjoy the extended golden-hour light.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – revisit a favorite spot or explore something missed. Suggested: a peaceful walk along the Appian Way (Via Appia Antica) for a completely different, bucolic side of Rome – ancient cobblestones, pine trees, and crumbling tombs. Alternatively, visit the stunning Baths of Caracalla (Terme di Caracalla) nearby, one of Rome's most impressive yet undervisited ancient sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel, check out, and pack. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping – recommended spots: Eataly (near Ostiense) for quality Italian food products, or the artisan shops around Campo de' Fiori for ceramics and prints. Head to the airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at a classic bar – cornetto al cioccolato and a double espresso (~€4)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch assembled from a local alimentari (deli) – prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, bread, and fruit (~€12–15 per person); enjoy it in a park or on the Appian Way
meals.dinner: Airport or in-transit meal, or an early dinner near the hotel before departure (~€20–25 per person at a neighborhood trattoria)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00–12:00) and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Rome's Fiumicino (FCO) airport is ~45 minutes by train (Leonardo Express, ~€14) or ~60–90 minutes by taxi (~€48 fixed rate from central Rome). Allow extra time for summer travel congestion. Keep €20–30 in cash for tips, nasoni water, and small vendors.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino (or Ciampino) airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighbourhood to get your bearings. Pick up a gelato from a nearby artisan gelateria to ease into the Roman pace.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – Join an intimate guided evening walk through Trastevere's cobblestone streets, sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, local wines, and cured meats. The golden-hour light on the medieval facades makes this the perfect soft introduction to Rome's culinary soul. Tour typically runs 18:30–21:30.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: N/A – in-flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Included tastings on the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk; supplement with a sit-down finale at Ristorante Paris (Trastevere) – a Roman institution serving cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara in an elegant setting.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private airport transfer and the Trastevere food tour well in advance. Keep luggage light for the evening walk. Wear comfortable walking shoes – cobblestones can be uneven. Weather: expect ~29°C and low rain probability; a light linen layer for the evening is sufficient.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Begin with an exclusive early-access (08:00 opening) skip-the-line guided tour of one of the world's greatest art collections. A private art historian guide leads you through the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminates in an awe-inspiring, less-crowded viewing of Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling. Allow 3–3.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross St. Peter's Square and explore St. Peter's Basilica at your own pace (free entry). Climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome. Afterwards, head to the Prati neighbourhood – the upscale district just outside the Vatican walls – for a leisurely lunch and a browse of its elegant boutiques and antique print shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest during the hottest part of the late afternoon, then head out for a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar (e.g., Settimo at the Waldorf Astoria Rome or Il Sorpasso in Prati). Follow with a refined dinner in the Prati area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a classic Roman bar – cornetto and cappuccino at Caffè San Pietro (near the Vatican).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Angelo (Prati) – a beloved neighbourhood trattoria serving authentic Roman pasta dishes at a premium-casual level; book ahead.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Sorpasso (Prati) or upgrade to Ristorante Il Matriciano – a historic Roman restaurant favoured by artists and intellectuals, serving impeccable Roman classics.

day_by_day.notes: Early-access Vatican tours sell out months in advance – book immediately. Dress code for St. Peter's Basilica: covered shoulders and knees required. Carry a refillable water bottle; Rome's 'nasoni' street fountains offer free, clean drinking water throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Take a private taxi or chauffeured car to the Villa Borghese park for a timed-entry (09:00) guided tour of the Borghese Gallery. Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases in an intimate, palazzo setting. Entry is strictly timed to 2 hours – savour every room.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the manicured Villa Borghese gardens – Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax in the shade. Descend via the Spanish Steps to the Tridente neighbourhood. Explore the Via Condotti luxury shopping strip (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi) and visit the Trevi Fountain (best in the early afternoon before peak crowds). Toss your coin.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at a chic bar near the Pantheon, then dinner in the historic centre.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel's restaurant or at the iconic Antico Caffè Greco on Via Condotti – Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), a favourite of Keats, Byron, and Goethe.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nino (Via Borgognona, Tridente) – a Florentine-Roman institution beloved by the fashion crowd; excellent bistecca and pasta.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Convivio Troiani (near Piazza Navona) – one of Rome's finest Michelin-starred restaurants, offering creative Italian haute cuisine in a 16th-century palazzo. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be pre-booked (they sell out weeks ahead); only 360 visitors allowed per 2-hour slot. The gallery does not allow re-entry. Wear light, breathable clothing – June afternoons reach ~30°C. The walk from Borghese to the Spanish Steps is downhill and very pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Join a private guided archaeological walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. Begin on the Palatine Hill (birthplace of Rome, home of emperors' palaces) with sweeping views over the Forum below, then descend into the Roman Forum itself – the Via Sacra, Temple of Saturn, Arch of Titus. Your expert guide brings 2,000 years of history vividly to life. Start at 08:30 to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit near the Colosseum for an optional exterior photo stop (or add a Colosseum interior visit with your guide). Head to the Aventine Hill – a quiet, aristocratic neighbourhood – to visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole (a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome) and the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for panoramic views over Rome. Rest at the hotel during peak afternoon heat (13:30–16:00).
day_by_day.evening: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour (evening version or a curated private dinner experience in Testaccio). Alternatively, explore the Testaccio neighbourhood independently – Rome's authentic working-class culinary district – for a memorable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a neighbourhood bar near the Forum.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Aroma (rooftop of Palazzo Manfredi, directly overlooking the Colosseum) – one of Rome's most spectacular dining settings with Michelin-starred cuisine. An unmissable luxury experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) – a beloved Roman trattoria carved into Monte dei Cocci (a hill of ancient amphora shards), serving definitive versions of cacio e pepe, carbonara, and coda alla vaccinara.

day_by_day.notes: The Forum/Palatine combined ticket also includes the Colosseum – decide in advance whether to add the interior. Book Ristorante Aroma weeks ahead; request a Colosseum-view table. Testaccio is a short taxi ride from the Aventine Hill. Saturday evenings in Testaccio are lively and authentic.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Spend Sunday morning at the Mercato Testaccio, Rome's most authentic covered food market. A knowledgeable local guide introduces you to Roman culinary heritage: sample offal preparations (trippa, pajata), aged pecorino, supplì, fresh pasta, and seasonal produce. Engage with the vendors – many families have traded here for generations. Market is at its best 08:00–13:00 on Sundays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pyramid of Cestius (a genuine ancient Egyptian-style pyramid in the middle of Rome) and the adjacent Protestant Cemetery – one of Rome's most serene and moving spots, where Keats and Shelley are buried. Then take a private car to the Trastevere neighbourhood for a relaxed afternoon: browse artisan workshops, independent bookshops, and the Sunday flea market at Porta Portese (one of Europe's largest, open until 14:00).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk across the Ponte Sisto bridge to the Campo de' Fiori area. Enjoy a Negroni at a terrace bar as the piazza transitions from market to evening social hub. Dinner in the Jewish Ghetto – one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric neighbourhoods.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market tour – the tour itself includes substantial tastings.
meals.lunch: Post-market lunch at Da Remo (Testaccio) – Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio and pizza tonda spot, beloved by locals. Casual but iconic.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nonna Betta (Jewish Ghetto) – the finest Jewish-Roman cuisine in Rome: carciofi alla giudia (deep-fried artichokes), baccalà in dolceforte, and ricotta-based desserts in an intimate, warmly lit setting.

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese flea market closes at 14:00 – arrive by 10:00 for the best finds. The Jewish Ghetto is a 10-minute walk from Campo de' Fiori. Sunday is a wonderful day to explore Trastevere and the Ghetto as many tourist groups are at the Vatican. Carry cash for the market and flea market.

day_by_day.morning: Private Art & Architecture Deep Dive – Dedicate the morning to Rome's Baroque masterpieces with a private art historian. Visit the Church of San Luigi dei Francesi (Caravaggio's St. Matthew cycle), Sant'Agostino (another Caravaggio), and Santa Maria della Vittoria (Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa). These are free to enter and, with a knowledgeable guide, profoundly rewarding. Finish at Piazza Navona – Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers – for a coffee at the historic Caffè della Pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pantheon (book timed entry in advance – now requires a ticket) – one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Spend time in the surrounding neighbourhood: the elegant Piazza della Rotonda, the nearby Piazza della Minerva (Bernini's elephant obelisk). Then visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj – a private aristocratic palace-gallery still owned by the Doria Pamphilj family, housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. Largely overlooked by tourists – a true hidden gem.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell aperitivo at a rooftop terrace with views over the Roman skyline (e.g., Terrazza Borromini at Palazzo Pamphilj or the rooftop of the Hotel Raphael). Splurge on a grand final dinner at one of Rome's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Caffè Sant'Eustachio (near the Pantheon) – widely considered Rome's finest espresso. Order the gran caffè (pre-sweetened, their signature preparation).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante La Rosetta (near the Pantheon) – Rome's most prestigious seafood restaurant, serving impeccably fresh Mediterranean fish and shellfish in an elegant setting.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel, Monte Mario) – Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, helmed by Chef Heinz Beck. Extraordinary tasting menu, impeccable wine list, and panoramic views over the entire city. Reserve months in advance; jacket required.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the culinary pinnacle of Rome – this reservation should be made as early as possible, ideally at the time of trip booking. The Palazzo Doria Pamphilj audio guide is narrated by a current family member – charming and personal. Pantheon tickets must be pre-booked online.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Rome – Rise early for one last espresso ritual at a neighbourhood bar. Take a peaceful early-morning walk to a favourite piazza – perhaps the Piazza del Popolo or the Pincian Hill terrace above it – before the city fully wakes. Visit any last-minute shops for artisan gifts: leather goods on Via della Croce, gourmet provisions at Volpetti (Testaccio) or Roscioli Salumeria (Campo de' Fiori) – pick up aged pecorino, truffle products, or Roman biscotti to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch before your private transfer to the airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure – Arrivederci, Roma.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at a local bar: cornetto integrale and a perfectly pulled ristretto.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Roscioli Ristorante (near Campo de' Fiori) – a celebrated deli-restaurant hybrid with an extraordinary wine cellar, serving exceptional Roman pasta, cured meats, and cheese. One of Rome's most beloved institutions.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer the evening before. Volpetti and Roscioli are excellent for vacuum-packed provisions that travel well. Check airline liquid/food import restrictions for your return destination. Leave a generous tip for any guides or drivers who made the week exceptional – it is customary and appreciated.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago
